data.narrative:
Arbor Energy, led by founder Brad Hartwig, is a Series A-stage climate and energy company seeking valuation following $96M in total capital raised. The relevant comp universe consists of one public company and eight private peers operating in the Climate & Energy sector, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The stage-progression method was the only applicable valuation approach. Using total raised ($96M) as a proxy for current valuation and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier for advancement from Series A to the next financing stage yields an implied valuation of $192M. The peer-median method was not applicable; while eight same-sector peers exist, insufficient datapoints met narrow filtering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier), and a cross-sector median would lack relevant precision.

The triangulation analysis, derived from one method, supports a median valuation of $192M, with a low estimate of $163M and high estimate of $221M reflecting reasonable bounds around the stage-progression calculation. Key uncertainties limiting this analysis include the sparse comparable set, reliance on a single valuation method, and absence of company-specific financial metrics or operational milestones. Validation would benefit from identifying additional same-stage or adjacent-stage private comparables in the energy technology space, or obtaining forward revenue/growth assumptions specific to Arbor Energy's business model.
